originalTitle: Bajaj Finance posts 28% growth in net profit amid healthy loan demand
simplifiedContent: Bajaj Finance, a finance company, made 28% more profit in the June quarter compared to the same time last year. This is likely because many people are borrowing money from them, which is a good sign for their business. The company now manages a large amount of money, ₹5.47 lakh crore, which is 24% more than before, and they also got 5.1 million new customers. Their income from interest on loans increased by 23%, which is another positive sign. This growth suggests that Bajaj Finance is doing well and expects to give out many more new loans in the future.

originalTitle: Korea’s leverage trap has an echo in India
simplifiedContent: In India, many individual investors are borrowing a lot of money from brokers to buy stocks, which can be a risky thing to do. This is creating a potential problem for the whole financial system, because if the stock market goes down, these investors might not be able to pay back their loans. The amount of borrowed money, or "margin debt", has increased a lot, partly because new brokers are competing with each other to lend to investors. This is similar to a situation that happened in Korea, but in India, the borrowed money is being used to buy stocks that other investors are actually trying to avoid. This makes things tricky for the people in charge of the economy, who are already dealing with inflation and a weakening currency.

originalTitle: Sebi opens faster route for rollout of AIF plans
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has made it easier for companies to launch new investment plans, called Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs). They've introduced a new system called GARUDA, which allows companies to launch their plans faster. Normally, companies have to wait, but now they can launch their plans just 10 days after filing some paperwork. This change will help new investment plans become available to investors more quickly. This matters because it can give investors more options and opportunities to put their money into different types of investments.

originalTitle: Stocks to watch: Maruti Suzuki, IOC, Tata Steel among shares in focus today; check list here
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the two main Indian stock market indexes, Sensex and Nifty 50, went up a bit on Thursday. Sensex rose by 274 points (0.35%) to 77,928, and Nifty 50 rose by 67 points (0.28%) to 24,317. This means that the overall value of the stocks in these indexes increased slightly. As a result, some stocks like Maruti Suzuki, IOC, and Tata Steel might be worth paying attention to today. These movements can be important to investors who own these stocks or are thinking of buying or selling them.

originalTitle: Curtains down on co-location, dark fibre: Sebi agrees to NSE's  ₹1,491 crore settlement
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market regulator, Sebi, has agreed to a settlement with the National Stock Exchange (NSE) for ₹1,491 crore. This settlement ends a long-running legal dispute between Sebi and NSE. The dispute was related to issues called "co-location" and "dark fibre", but the details of these issues aren't important - what matters is that the settlement is now done. This settlement is significant because it allows NSE to move forward with listing its own shares on the stock market, which is a big step for the company. The settlement brings closure to the issue and allows NSE to focus on its future plans.
